parsed.reason: This message satisfies all requirements for an "optin" kind. It states there are other Hale families nearby, explains that introductions happen only when there's a genuinely good match, and crucially reassures the parent upfront that nothing is shared with either side until both agree—answering the parent's unasked question "what did you tell them" before they have to ask it. It includes the opt-out mechanism ("Worth having me keep an eye out?"). The speaker is first-person singular ("I can make an introduction"), not "Hale" or "we/us/our". It avoids announcement voice, exclamation marks, and instructions on what to type back. The tone is measured and treats the offer as small. Grammar is correct throughout. It contains no facts beyond what an optin requires—no names, neighborhoods, or child details—and reads as a competent, human-scaled message from someone raising something minor.
